participants: Josh Lyons (mastermind leader, running the session)
Ben Byrne (Primal Instinct closer, attending as a member)
summary: Not a Primal Instinct call at all. This is a roughly two-hour group training session of a third-party high-ticket sales mastermind run by Josh Lyons and referred to as UCM, with an unnamed figure called 'UM' or the Underground Mentor above him. Ben Byrne attends as a paying member and speaks twice — once in the wins round, where he mentions Primal by name ('Trevor's the guy I'm selling for this new fitness offer'), and once to endorse the session's main theme. The session has three parts: a short training on holding state when a prospect opens hostile and demands the price up front; a long culture address in which Lyons argues that top closers are born rather than made, announces he will stop accommodating slower members and expects a 'culling'; and call reviews of two other members' recorded prospect calls from entirely unrelated businesses. None of the sales content concerns Primal Instinct, kettlebells, or any Primal prospect.
notable: This file is in the Ben Byrne rep folder of the Primal call corpus but contains no Primal prospect and no Primal business. It must not enter any Primal denominator, sales or internal-coaching.

The recording captures verbatim playback of two other companies' recorded sales calls, including named prospects and their private business and health information — one prospect's monthly net profit figures and salary, and a disclosure that 'last year in May, I found out that I had atrial fibrillation. I was in hospital for a week.' Those individuals are not Primal prospects and this material is now sitting in Primal's Drive.

Direct coaching to maximise pressure on a prospect: 'Put as much pressure on as you can' and 'I want to put the pressure on him more, and I would have used a shorter timeline to do that.' Ben Byrne is a member being trained in this method, and a Primal prospect complained the same week about feeling pushed on a closing call.

Unauthorised use of a company credit card is held up as exemplary: 'She used the company credit card to join the mastermind, as in a unicorn just finds a solution ... A unicorn asks for forgiveness, not for permission.'

Lyons's stated thesis is that closer ability is innate and fixed: 'when we are conceived, we are conceived with a destiny, and that can't be changed ... it was written, I believe it was written before the day you were born.' He tells members in the bottom category they are 'probably just, no disrespect, never going to be a unicorn' and 'you're welcome to leave'.

He announced a policy change to cut call reviews off after one minute if the rep is 'out of state', and predicted and welcomed member attrition — 'it will be another UM calls them the cullings where like some people, I'm just going to leave. And that's totally fine.'

Members and prospects are repeatedly described in derogatory terms during the culture address, including 'maybe I can like just save the retards', 'yeah, dumbass', and 'they'll sit there crying like a big baby'. Lyons also embraces the cult framing directly: 'This feels like a cult, so off then, of course it's a cult.'

One genuinely useful counter-point is taught: Lyons rejects the industry framing of 'sales resistance' because it makes the prospect the enemy — 'We never point the finger and say the prospect's the problem ... The enemy is you.' He also coaches leading with empathy over confrontation: 'we lead with honey, not with the stick.'

Ben Byrne's own contribution is about standards slipping as the group grew, not about Primal technique: 'the longer I've been in it, as more and more new people have come in, that that standard has definitely been slipping with some people.'

Context for the corpus: Ben mentions he is newly selling the Primal offer, following Trevor's programme himself, and 'starting to close deals now'. This dates his tenure and is useful when reading his adherence scores.
